# Syrtis v1.0.0

**Within what v1 covers, the Windows app has caught up with the macOS app: more quota sources and accounts, a window card that places each window the same way, and the same keyboard shortcuts.** The changes you are most likely to notice from v0.6.0: Ctrl+1–9 and Ctrl+[ / ] now switch between Overview and the client tabs instead of between lenses; setup cards appear once on the Overview in place of the Discord card that used to open at startup; and agy started by Syrtis no longer updates itself.

## More quota sources and accounts

- **Claude Desktop.** When Claude Desktop is signed in, its account gets its own quota card. If it is the same account as your Claude Code login, the two show as one card. Syrtis does not renew Desktop's sign-in; when it expires the card says so.
- **More than one Claude account.** Settings → General → Claude accounts → Add config dir… adds a Claude Code config folder. Each folder gets its own quota card, its usage counts toward your totals, and its window usage stays with that account. Folders on a drive letter work, including a mapped network drive; `\\server\share` and WSL paths can't be added.
- **A Claude `setup-token` without restarting.** `CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN` is read from your Windows environment variables on every refresh, so setting or removing it takes effect at the next refresh. A token set only in one terminal's session is no longer picked up.
- **Kiro**, read from the Kiro IDE sign-in.
- **OpenCode Go**, with its rolling, weekly and monthly windows on the OpenCode tab.
- **Grok Bot.** Its weekly quota now appears, and Grok Build and Grok Bot share one "Grok Build & Bot" tab. When the Grok Bot desktop app is signed in, its sign-in is used only after you press Allow on its card; when it is signed out, Syrtis reads the Cursor IDE sign-in instead. Settings → Dashboard → Agent limits → "Use Grok Bot's sign-in" takes that permission back. Either answer refreshes the card and the tray right away.
- **Antigravity accounts.** Settings → General → Antigravity accounts → "Capture current agy login" stores agy's current account in Windows Credential Manager. While agy is still on that account it shows on the main Antigravity card; once agy switches to another account, the captured one gets a card of its own. Capturing every account agy signs in to is a separate switch and is off until you turn it on. A paid Google AI plan now shows its name instead of "Free".
- **The OpenCode tab shows the subscriptions opencode routes through**, such as Codex and Copilot, under "↔ Routes through opencode". Switching off opencode's own card keeps those cards.

## The window card and the Quota lens

- **Account pills.** When a client has more than one account with a live window, pills above the window tabs switch between them, and the choice is remembered. The main account's pill shows its email when known.
- **Model-only weekly limits**, such as a Claude weekly limit for one model, now appear, and their bars and history count only that model.
- **Windows are placed the way macOS places them.** A window that has ended no longer stays on screen as "Resets in now". After a reset the card says "Placing the window…" until your local usage has been read, then shows the window as idle or as an inferred window starting at your first message. A client on its first window fills in its usage bars without waiting for a recorded window.
- When Syrtis can't tell which local usage belongs to an account, its card says "Local usage can't be attributed to this account yet." instead of showing another account's numbers.
- When the window's quota report has an error, the window card shows that error instead of the last windows it had.
- The history strip and heatmap say "Quota history could not be read" only when the latest read failed and the client has no window drawn, and they leave out clients whose tab or Agent limits card you have hidden.
- Right after Syrtis starts, before the first quota refresh, these cards show your saved history (hidden clients excluded) instead of waiting empty.

## The Agent limits card

- Codex, Claude, Gemini, Grok Build and Grok Bot get a card before their first reading ("Checking…", then "No data"). An unconfigured Claude card explains how to set it up, with commands you can copy.
- Cards follow your tab order; on the Overview, drag a card by its ⠿ handle to reorder both. Each card shows the account's email and plan under its name and a status badge, and a window with enough history gets a trend arrow.
- A card that fails to refresh keeps its last bars under the error.
- Settings → Dashboard → Agent limits has a switch for each client's card, and "Show Agent limits card" turns the whole card off.

## Dashboard and tray

- **Keyboard:** Ctrl+1 opens Overview and Ctrl+2–9 the client tabs in order; Ctrl+[ and Ctrl+] step to the previous and next tab. Hold Ctrl to see the numbers on the tabs. Ctrl+G cycles the Token Usage card through Bars, a full-year Heatmap, and 3D. Lenses are picked with the lens buttons.
- **Drag a client tab** in the flyout to reorder the tab row.
- **First-run setup cards** on the Overview walk through agents on this PC, the menu-bar icon and text, pace, usage attribution, start at login, and Discord. "Skip setup" dismisses them. The Discord card only opens Settings; Discord stays off unless you turn it on in Settings → General → Discord.
- Settings → Dashboard → Overview cards hides individual Overview cards.
- **Sand shoal**, a new tray icon style (Settings → Menu bar → Tray icon), and a Light / Moderate / Heavy animation pace. A tray reading older than 30 minutes turns grey, and a quota source that stops reporting shows a crossed-out gauge instead of its last percentage.
- The header shows the Syrtis mark and wordmark, the footer names the open lens, and a small light beside the live rate flickers while tokens flow.
- The Models lens shows each model's share of cost and its input / output / cache split. Expanding a day or month lists one row per model.
- After a cold start the dashboard shows your last data, up to 90 days old, until the fresh scan arrives; the Refresh button's tooltip says how old it is (for example, "2d ago").

## Also in this release

- agy started by Syrtis for the Antigravity quota now runs with its auto-update turned off, so it no longer starts agy's background updater, which could open a Windows Terminal window. agy you run in a terminal still updates itself.
- When an agy quota check times out, the card says agy was probably waiting for a sign-in.
- The usage engine is updated. It adds ZCode, Augment Code, Hindsight, Muse Code, Reasonix, Kimchi, Senpi and Oh My Pi (counted separately from Pi), counts Kimi Work sessions as Kimi, and recovers Pi transcripts it used to skip, so Pi, Oh My Pi and Kimi totals can change. It prices Kiro credits and corrects model prices: Claude Fable 5.1 and Claude Opus 5.5 cost about a sixth less, while some models now charge for cache writes.
- Syrtis no longer turns on Windows Efficiency Mode for its tray icon, which had put the whole app at idle priority.
- A clock that jumped backwards no longer erases quota history; only readings stamped in the future are dropped.
- Long model names and account labels are shortened in the middle, hover tooltips stay inside the visible area, and card headers no longer cut a long window name first.
- More Simplified and Traditional Chinese translations, the app's own name in place of "TokenBar" in a few messages, and About now credits CodexBar and RunCat.
